findings.summary: The associated statements used 251 ms of database time over the 4 minutes since statistics were reset (17%). Deleting a row from public.customers, or changing its key, makes the database look for matching rows in public.orders (20K rows) without an index, which means reading the whole table. Queries that load orders rows for one customers row can't seek either. The statements that go through it take 17% of database time.

impact.label: 251 ms of database time over the 4 minutes since statistics were reset (17%)

findings.summary: 251 ms of database time over the 4 minutes since statistics were reset (17%). One query plans to read public.orders and keep only those matching `(orders.customer_id = $1)`. The captured scan uses 20K rows as its size basis; this scan's catalog reports 20K rows in the table. Captured estimates can predate the current table size. No index starts with customer_id, so the database has no faster way in. It accounts for 17% of database time. customer_id is also the foreign key to customers, so deletes there scan this table too.
findings.title: orders is read in full to find rows by customer_id
